title: 10 Best business phone systems for accounting firms
summary: Looking for business phone systems for accounting firms? We compare 10 options on texting, call recording, shared numbers, and pricing to help you choose.
body_markdown:
Tax season means weeks of nonstop calls about refunds, extensions, and IRS letters. When those calls and texts live in different places, it’s easy for a new lead to slip through or for a client to end up repeating their story to a second person.


A good VoIP phone system keeps calls and texts in one place. When a client calls back, anyone on your team can see past conversations instead of asking them to explain it all again. You respond faster and get back to prospects before they choose another firm.


In this guide, we compare 10 of the best business phone systems for accounting firms. We’ll look at their pros, cons, and pricing to help you choose the right one.


##


Solutions roundup


Here’s a quick look at 10 business phone systems and what each one is best for:


1. **Quo:** Best for growing firms that need calls, texts, and client context in one AI-powered platform


2. **RingCentral:** Best for large firms that need desk phones


3. **Nextiva:** Best for midsized firms that talk to clients by phone, email, live chat, and social media


4. **Dialpad:** Best for firms with a lot of international clients


5. **Ooma:** Best for calling clients across North America


6. **Grasshopper:** Best for firms that need a phone menu with multi-digit extensions


7. **8×8:** Best for firms with high call volumes


8. **Zoom Phone:** Best for firms that already use Zoom


9. **eVoice:** Best for firms that want the option of a live receptionist


10. **Google Voice:** Best for firms that already use Google Workspace

### **1. Quo: Best business phone solution for growing accounting firms**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calling and messaging to the US and Canada
- Business-friendly pricing
- AI-powered call summaries
- Shared inboxes for team calls and texts
- Internal threads for private discussions about clients
- Auto-replies and scheduled texts
- Integrations with Zoho CRM, HubSpot, Salesforce, and more


#### Cons


- No verification through two-factor authentication*


**Nearly all virtual phone numbers share this problem. Companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you authenticate accounts through a virtual phone number.*


Quo is a modern business phone system that helps accounting firms manage client calls and texts in one place. Your team can use it on the phones and computers you already have without buying new equipment.


Hector Bilbao, Principal at Real Tax Advisors LLC, said:


“ *I have tried multiple online phone companies, including Google Voice and Grasshopper. The very best one has been Quo, due to how easy it is and how many features it has, including knowing who on my team has called or texted a client right on the conversation view.* ”


Quo’s shared inboxes let your staff see past calls and texts with clients. When a client calls back, the person answering can review previous conversations and pick up where things left off. Staff can also use internal threads to discuss client requests privately and leave notes for colleagues.


If your team can’t answer a call,[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) , Quo’s AI receptionist, can step in 24/7. You can train it to answer common questions about your firm’s fees and services. Sona can also transfer callers to the right person, whether they need help with a personal tax return or business financing. It records the calls it handles and provides summaries with next steps, so your staff can follow up without listening to every recording.


Each user gets a free local or toll-free number with unlimited calls and texts to the US and Canada. You can also port an existing local US or Canadian number or a North American toll-free number at no cost.


See how Quo works for your firm with a[seven-day free trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) .


#### Key features of Quo


- Sona, the AI receptionist
- Local, vanity, and[toll-free numbers](https://www.quo.com/toll-free-numbers)
- Free number porting
- [Shared phone numbers](https://www.quo.com/product/shared-numbers)
- Shared contacts and contact notes
- Phone menus, also known as[IVR](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/ivr)
- Voicemail to email
- Group messaging
- Manual or automatic[call recording](https://www.quo.com/product/call-recording)
- [AI call summaries and transcripts](https://www.quo.com/features/call-transcriptions)
- AI call tags
- 9,000+[integrations](https://www.quo.com/integrations) through Zapier and Make


#### **Quo pricing**


[Quo’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/pricing) includes three plans:


- **Starter:** $15 per user per month for unlimited US and Canada calls and texts, one local or toll-free number per user, voicemail transcripts, manual call recording, shared numbers for up to 10 users, and more
- **Business:** $23 per user per month for unlimited users on shared numbers, AI call summaries and transcripts, phone menus, automatic call recording, integrations with Zoho CRM and HubSpot, and more
- **Scale:** $35 per user per month for AI call tags, dedicated onboarding, inbound phone support, and priority chat and email support


Every plan includes enough Sona credits for 10 calls a month at no extra cost. If your phones get busier, Sona’s paid plans start at $25 per month for up to 40 calls.


### **2. RingCentral: Best choice for renting desk phones**


#### Pros


- Desk phone rentals are available on every plan
- Video meetings are built-in
- Unlimited calls to the US and Canada


#### Cons


- Desk phone rentals require multi-year contracts
- Base plan only includes 25 texts per user per month
- Call recordings are deleted after 90 days


[RingCentral](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-alternatives/) makes sense if your accounting firm prefers desk phones, since you can rent them on even the entry-level Core plan. However, desk phone rentals require a contract of at least two years. That’s a long commitment if your team decides to switch to mobile and desktop apps sooner.


The Core plan includes unlimited calls to the US and Canada, 100 toll-free minutes, and 25 texts per user each month. Unlimited calling is useful, but the texting limit could be a problem. A few conversations with clients about missing tax forms or filing deadlines can use up those 25 messages.


You also get on-demand call recording, voicemail transcripts, and voicemail-to-email on Core. These features help your team keep records of client conversations. But RingCentral[deletes call recordings after 90 days](https://support.ringcentral.com/article-v2/RingCentral-data-retention-policies.html?brand=RingCentral&product=RingEX&language=en_US) on every plan. If your firm needs to keep them longer, you’ll have to download them or use an archiving tool.


Some customers have had technical and billing issues with RingCentral. Here are a couple of the latest reviews we found:


*“* Very disappointed with RingCentral. We’ve experienced poor phone service, billing problems, and incoming calls that don’t even ring. As a business, we depend on customers being able to reach us, and this service has been frustrating and unreliable.” —[Verified user on Trustpilot](https://ca.trustpilot.com/reviews/6ae39769c7ee892210f3c4ce)


*“* I have been using RingCentral in our small medical practice, and it has been very problematic. Slow to respond, repeatedly does not show text messages sent or received, and it frequently refuses to send text messages. I have gone to “Help?” and all you get is a chat bot that runs in circles.” —[Verified user on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/ringcentral-contact-center/reviews/ringcentral-contact-center-review-13119314)


### Key features of RingCentral


**


- Desk and conference phone rentals
- Shared phone numbers for calls
- Multi-level auto-attendant for routing client calls
- On-demand call recording
- Voicemail transcriptions
- AI call transcriptions and summaries


### RingCentral pricing


**


There are several[RingEX pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-pricing/) plans to choose from:


- **Core:** $20 per user per month for unlimited calls in the US and Canada, on-demand call recording, AI-powered call notes, 25 texts, 100 pooled toll-free minutes, and video meetings
- **Advanced:** $25 per user per month for automatic call recording, CRM integrations, unlimited online faxing, 100 texts, and 1,000 pooled toll-free minutes
- **Ultra:** $35 per user per month for 10,000 pooled toll-free minutes, 200 texts, and unlimited storage space for files and call recordings
- **AI Customer Engagement Bundle with AIR:** Custom pricing for an AI receptionist, 200 texts, 10,000 pooled toll-free minutes, unlimited storage, a shared text inbox, and ready-made text replies
- **AI Customer Engagement Bundle with AIR and ACE:** Custom pricing for AI-powered call scoring, staff coaching, and reports on team performance


You can also get some AI Customer Engagement Bundle features without switching plans. RingCentral’s Business SMS Booster starts at $25 per month for shared text inboxes and ready-made text replies. For $35 per month, the Call Queues Booster lets clients on hold request a callback instead of waiting.


### **3. Nextiva: Best phone system for omnichannel communications**


#### Pros


- Calls, texts, email, chat, and social messages in one place
- Unlimited calls in the US and Canada
- Desktop and mobile apps


#### Cons


- Only 100 texts per user per month on the base plan
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- CRM integrations cost extra
- Real-time transcription is only available on the highest-tier plan


[Nextiva](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-alternatives/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) is a business phone system for firms that communicate with clients across different channels. It lets you manage calls, texts, emails, social media messages, and live chat in one app. You can make unlimited calls to the US, Canada, and Puerto Rico.


Texting is where Nextiva falls short for your firm. Its entry-level plan includes only 100 texts per user each month. If your team regularly texts clients about missing documents and appointments, you can reach that limit quickly. You’ll also need to upgrade for call recording and real-time transcription.


Nextiva doesn’t offer a free trial either. You can book a demo, but you can’t test the system with your own team before signing up.


Some Nextiva customers have reported issues with the level of their customer support. One reviewer in particular was unhappy with the support team’s responsiveness:


*“Be very careful with this company. Once you are set up, it is near impossible to get support. More than 3 times I waited on hold for over 1 hour and eventually had to hang up because I got through to no one. A simple billing fix has taken over a month to try and resolve.”* —[Verified user on Trustpilot](https://ca.trustpilot.com/reviews/698b8b961883e35f3b30690d)


### Key features of Nextiva


**


- Unlimited calls and video meetings
- Team messaging
- Email messaging
- Auto-attendant for routing calls
- Shared team inbox
- Desktop, web, and mobile apps


### Nextiva pricing


**


Here’s what to expect from[Nextiva pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-pricing/) :


- **Core:** $15 per user per month for unlimited calls in the US and Canada, 100 texts, video meetings with screen sharing, voicemail transcription, and team chat
- **Engage:** $25 per user per month for call recording, a toll-free number with 2,000 minutes, 500 texts, a shared text inbox, and live chat
- **Scale:** $75 per user per month for real-time call transcription, AI call notes and summaries, unlimited texts, and skills-based call routing


You can add Nextiva’s AI receptionist, XBert, to any plan starting at $99 per month. That covers 100 calls, texts, or chats that it resolves on its own.


### **4. Dialpad: Best phone system for calling international customers**


#### Pros


- Local phone numbers in 50+ countries
- Unlimited calling to the US and Canada
- Real-time call transcription and voicemail transcription


#### Cons


- Only 250 outbound texts included per user per month
- International texts incur additional charges
- Salesforce and HubSpot integrations require an upgrade
- Some users report dropped calls and connection issues


[Dialpad](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-alternatives/) is a cloud phone system for mid-sized and larger accounting firms with international clients. It lets your firm get local phone numbers in more than 50 countries. A client in London or Sydney can call a local number instead of paying international rates to reach you. You also get unlimited calls across the US and Canada. Toll-free numbers cost extra at $15 a month each, plus $0.02 per minute for incoming calls.


There are some limits to consider, though.[Dialpad SMS](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-sms/) only includes 250 outbound texts per user each month, and it doesn’t let you buy additional phone numbers. If your team needs a second line for a new office or service, you’ll have to move up a tier.


Dialpad also connects to CRMs like HubSpot and Microsoft Dynamics 365. However, some users have had trouble getting the HubSpot integration to work properly. One user said:


*“It did not integrate well with HubSpot CRM — calls would go missing, not attached to the account we are calling off it. It just was not connected to HubSpot well.”* —[Verified user on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/dialpad-connect/reviews/dialpad-connect-review-13086705)


Another said the integration seemed to create duplicate contacts:


*“The integration with HubSpot has not been the best. I’m not a fan of how contacts are managed when working with a team. Seems to create duplicates too often.”* —[Verified user on](https://www.g2.com/products/dialpad-connect/reviews/dialpad-connect-review-13086705)[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/dialpad-connect/reviews/dialpad-connect-review-7668631)


### Key features of Dialpad


**


- Unlimited calls to the US and Canada
- AI call summaries and action items
- Custom call routing and ring groups
- Call recording
- Call forwarding and three-way calling
- Team messaging


### Dialpad pricing


**


[Dialpad Connect pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-pricing/) breaks down into three plans:


- **Standard:** $15 per user per month for unlimited calls in the US and Canada, texting, call forwarding and routing, manual call recording, AI call transcripts and summaries, and voicemail transcription
- **Pro:** $25 per user per month for automatic recording on shared lines and Salesforce and HubSpot integrations
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing for larger firms with unlimited office locations and a 100% uptime guarantee


Additional phone numbers, toll-free numbers, and online faxing cost extra on every plan. International calls and texts may also come with usage charges.


### **5. Ooma: Best business phone for calling Puerto Rico and Mexico**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calls in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico
- Free toll-free number
- Online faxing on every plan


#### Cons


- Only 500 toll-free minutes per month
- No texting on the base plan
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- Desktop calling requires an upgrade


[Ooma](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-alternatives/) is a business phone system for accounting firms with clients across North America. With some providers, calling a client in Mexico can cost extra. Ooma’s base plan includes unlimited calls to the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico. You also get a free toll-free number with 500 minutes of incoming calls per month, but those minutes only apply to calls from within the US.


Ooma’s base plan doesn’t include texting, so you can’t send or receive client messages unless you upgrade. Voicemail transcription and call recording also require a higher-tier plan. You can use Ooma’s desktop app on the entry-level plan, but you’ll have to pay more to make calls directly from the app.


There are a number of Ooma customers who seem to be suffering from outages and dropped calls, based on the reviews they posted:


*“Very poor experience. The phone service has not been working for about six weeks, and customer support has been disappointing.” —*[Verified user on Trustpilot](https://ca.trustpilot.com/reviews/6acf9df472cabf6146b0af13)


*“Wireless phone service is not working. Spent 2 full days on the phone with customer support attempting to install the correct version with no success. Still dropping wi-fi connection and losing calls, which equals severe loss in business. Clientele is experiencing frustration contacting the office and unable to schedule appointments.” —*[Verified user on Trustpilot](https://ca.trustpilot.com/reviews/6ad93d6b3679bf41aa155242)


### Key features of Ooma


**


- Virtual receptionist and ring groups
- Call forwarding
- Virtual extensions
- Three-way calling
- Free number transfer
- Mobile app


### Ooma pricing


**


[Ooma pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-pricing/) include four options:


- **Essentials:** $19.95 per user per month for unlimited calls in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico, a virtual receptionist, a free toll-free number with 500 inbound minutes, and online faxing
- **Pro:** $24.95 per user per month for call recording, voicemail transcription, 250 texts per month with scheduled sending, video meetings with screen sharing, and desktop calling
- **Pro Plus:** $29.95 per user per month for QuickBooks Online and CRM integrations, AI call transcripts, 1,000 texts, online bookings, and call queuing
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing for Microsoft Teams integration, advanced analytics, and custom implementation


If your firm expects more calls during tax season, you can add 1,000 toll-free minutes for $15 per month. Ooma’s AI receptionist is available as a paid add-on.


### **6. Grasshopper: Best for businesses that need multi-digit extensions**


#### Pros


- Phone menu with extensions for different teams
- Unlimited users at a flat monthly price
- Voicemail transcription on every plan


#### Cons


- Only one user on the cheapest plan
- Just one included phone number until the highest-tier plan
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- Limited third-party integrations


[Grasshopper](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-alternatives/) is a business phone system for solo accountants and very small firms. Its entry-level plan, True Solo, only supports one user, with one phone number and one extension. Even so, you get unlimited calls to the US and Canada.


You can buy more numbers on True Solo, like a local number for clients in another city. But if you hire an assistant to handle client calls, you’ll need to upgrade.


Once you upgrade, you can add unlimited users for a flat monthly price instead of paying per person. You also get more extensions, call recording, and AI call summaries.


Grasshopper doesn’t offer saved text replies, though. If you’re regularly reminding clients to send missing tax documents, you’ll have to type those messages from scratch each time. It also has limited integrations, so call details won’t automatically sync with the other tools your firm uses.


Grasshopper users have reported difficulties canceling:


*“The software is terrible and hard to use, but what motivated me to leave a review is how difficult they make it to cancel their service. You can’t cancel through the website or the app. You have to call customer service and answer a bunch of questions. Then they put me on hold for 6 minutes while they were “canceling the account,” and they give BS excuses for why it is so hard to cancel the account.” —*[Verified user on G 2](https://www.g2.com/products/grasshopper/reviews/grasshopper-review-11312132)


Another customer who canceled reported difficulties getting his refund:


“ *I cancelled my account and requested a refund as they withdrew $464.78 from my account on June 25th, 2022. I called on that date, and they confirmed a refund. Fast forward to July 02, 2022, and the rep had no record of a refund OR a cancelled account. Grasshopper owes me almost half a grand. Called twice and was told both times a refund would be issued.” —*[Verified user on G](https://www.g2.com/products/grasshopper/reviews/grasshopper-review-11312132)[2](https://www.g2.com/products/grasshopper/reviews/grasshopper-review-6807200)


### Key features of Grasshopper


**


- Unlimited texting in the US and Canada
- Local and toll-free numbers
- Mobile and desktop apps
- Call forwarding
- Contact management
- Voicemail transcription and custom greetings


### Grasshopper pricing


**


Here’s how[Grasshopper pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-pricing/) compares across tiers:


- **True Solo:** $14 per month for one user, one phone number, and one extension
- **Solo Plus:** $25 per month for unlimited users, one phone number, three extensions, a phone menu, call recording, AI call summaries, and simultaneous call handling
- **Small Business:** $55 per month for unlimited users, four phone numbers, and unlimited extensions


### **7. 8×8: Best business phone for high call volumes**


#### Pros


- Callers can request a callback instead of waiting on hold
- Tools to monitor call volumes and staff performance
- SOC 2 Type 2 audited security


#### Cons


- No publicly listed pricing
- Advanced features can take time to learn
- Advanced analytics and some integrations cost extra


[8×8](https://www.quo.com/blog/8x8-alternatives/) offers a cloud phone system and contact center software for large accounting firms that handle a high volume of client calls. Its 8×8 Work app brings calls, texts, and video meetings into one place. Your team can use it on office computers or mobile phones when they’re away from their desks.


8×8 also offers AI tools for call analytics, post-call insights, and voicemail-to-text. You can use its AI Studio to build custom AI agents that answer common client questions.


8×8 doesn’t disclose its pricing online, so you’ll need to contact its sales team to find out how much these features will cost.


Some users have also reported problems with calls cutting out. One business owner said:


*“It cuts out incoming calls extremely frequently, which is a concern to the point that I have to give important clients a different contact number in case they call and are cut off.”* —[Verified user on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/8x8-work/reviews/8x8-work-review-11791091)


### Key features of 8×8


**


- Cloud fax
- Voicemail-to-email
- Auto-attendant and call routing
- Call recording
- HD video meetings for up to 10,000 participants
- AI call summaries and insights
- AI Studio for building custom AI agents


### 8×8 pricing


**


[8×8 pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/8x8-pricing/) isn’t publicly available. Contact its sales team directly for a quote.


### **8. Zoom Phone: Best phone system for Zoom users**


#### Pros


- Calls, Zoom meetings, and team chats in one app
- Call recording on every plan
- Voicemail transcription and AI call summaries


#### Cons


- Unlimited US and Canadian calling requires an upgrade
- Shared phone numbers are limited to 10 users and four simultaneous calls
- Team texting features require a paid add-on


[Zoom Phone](https://www.quo.com/blog/zoom-phone-alternatives/) is a business phone system that works alongside Zoom Workplace, the video meeting platform. You can make calls, send texts, check voicemail, and join video meetings from the Zoom app. Firms in the US and Canada can also text clients in both countries. Plus, Zoom Phone offers call recording on every plan, allowing you to keep a record of client conversations without paying for an upgrade.


However, some users have found Zoom Phone difficult to set up and customize. Here’s what one customer said:


*“The setup process was confusing, call routing and other functions \[are\] very unclear and hard to set up, customer service is completely non-existent.”* —[Verified user on Capterra](https://www.capterra.co.uk/reviews/208535/zoom-phone?overall_rating_ge=1#facets)


Zoom Phone also limits how your team can handle client messages. If clients text your main office number about missing documents, your staff can’t reply from that shared number without a paid add-on. And only 10 people can share one number, which won’t be enough for a growing firm.


### Key features of Zoom Phone


**


- SMS and MMS in the US and Canada
- Auto-attendants
- Call queues
- Business hours and holiday call routing
- Online fax
- Integrations with Slack, Microsoft, Google, and Salesforce


### Zoom Phone pricing


**


You can choose from five[Zoom Phone plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/zoom-phone-pricing/) :


- **US & Canada Metered:** $10.50 per user per month for pay-per-minute calls in the US and Canada, domestic texting, 50 fax pages per month, call recording, AI call summaries, and voicemail prioritization
- **US & Canada Unlimited:** $16 per user per month for unlimited calls in the US and Canada
- **Pro Plus:** $20.50 per user per month for meetings lasting up to 30 hours, local and cloud meeting recording with 10 GB of storage, unlimited AI meeting notes, and tools to organize and share videos
- **Business Plus:** $24.50 per user per month for meetings with up to 300 participants, unlimited online faxing, unlimited whiteboards, unlimited booking pages, SSO, and device management
- **Global Select:** $22 per user per month for one local phone number and unlimited domestic calls in one of 40+ supported countries and territories


Additional phone numbers cost $5 per month. Unlimited international calling to more than 15 countries and regions costs $10 per month.


### **9. eVoice: Best business phone for a live receptionist**


#### Pros


- Live receptionist is available as an add-on
- Auto-attendant is included in the base plan
- Straightforward pricing


#### Cons


- Unlimited texting in the US and Canada requires an upgrade
- Live receptionist only covers business hours
- Call recording and voicemail transcription cost extra
- Some users report a dated interface and limited integrations


[eVoice](https://www.quo.com/blog/evoice-alternatives/) is a legacy business phone system for small businesses. It offers unlimited calls in the US and Canada, advanced call handling, voicemail, and an auto-attendant on both its plans. Do you regularly text clients about appointments or missing documents? You’ll need the higher-tier Elite Plus plan for unlimited texting.


eVoice also offers a live receptionist who can answer client calls and book appointments. You can add the service to either plan or get it bundled with the phone system.


Before you sign up, know that the receptionists only work during business hours. For after-hours calls, look at other[small business answering services](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-ai-phone-answering-services/) .


The platform is also reportedly dated. One[verified user on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/evoice/reviews/evoice-review-12670120) said, “ *Bad UI. Too outdated. This can be improved.* ”


### Key features of eVoice


**


- Unlimited calls in the US and Canada
- Local and toll-free numbers
- Free number porting
- Multiple extensions
- Call routing
- Virtual fax
- Mobile app


### eVoice pricing


**


eVoice keeps it simple with two plans:


- **Elite:** $12 per month for unlimited calls in the US and Canada, local or toll-free numbers, free number porting, advanced call handling, and multiple extensions
- **Elite Plus:** $19 per month to add unlimited texting in the US and Canada from your business number


### **10. Google Voice: Best business phone for Google users**


#### Pros


- Free plan for personal use
- Unlimited calls and texts in the US
- Works with Gmail, Calendar, and Meet


#### Cons


- Can’t text clients outside the US
- No toll-free numbers or desktop app
- Doesn’t connect directly to CRMs or accounting software
- Teams need a paid Google Workspace subscription on top of Voice
- Google app integrations require a Google Voice for Business plan


[Google Voice](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-alternatives/) can work well for solo accountants in the US. Its free personal plan includes unlimited calls to the US and Canada. Recording client calls requires a paid plan, and you’ll need Standard or higher for an auto-attendant.


Google Voice makes the most sense for firms already using Google Workspace. It works with Gmail, Calendar, and Meet, so calls fit into the tools your team uses every day. But there are no[Google Voice integrations](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-integrations/) with third-party apps or an API to build your own. If your firm needs to connect its phone system to accounting software or a CRM, you may be better off looking elsewhere.


A[reviewer on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/google-voice/reviews/google-voice-review-11470708) said, *“Super simple and basic. Wasn’t able to do many “enhanced” things like keeping a text unread, or having auto-responses setup, etc. Worked great for just a small family business, but once we started to grow, we just needed something more robust.”*


### Key features of Google Voice


**


- Voicemail transcription
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- Auto-attendants and ring groups require an upgrade
- Call forwarding
- AI spam blocking
- Do not disturb synced to Google Calendar


### Google Voice pricing


**


Google Voice offers three individual plans and three team plans. Individual plans are only available to US customers, but businesses in 14 countries can sign up for team plans.


Here are the[Google Voice pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-pricing/) plans for individuals with no Workspace plan:


- **Basic:** Free for personal use, with unlimited domestic calling and texting
- **Starter:** $10 per month for call recording, three-way calling, and desk phone support
- **Standard:** $20 per month for AI note-taking and phone menus


Teams can choose from these Google Voice for Business with Workspace plans:


- **Starter:** $10 per user per month for up to 10 users with call recording, AI note-taking, and Google Meet and Calendar integration
- **Standard:** $20 per user per month with no user limit, ring groups, call queues, and phone menus
- **Premier:** $30 per user per month for automatic call recording, advanced reporting, and additional international phone numbers


Each user on these plans needs a paid Google Workspace subscription, which starts at $7 per user per month.


##


**How to pick the right business phone platform for your accounting firm**


Before choosing a phone system, use these questions to compare providers and figure out which one fits your firm’s needs.


**Pricing and contracts**


- Does the provider charge per user or per account?
- How much more will I pay if I hire additional staff during tax season?
- Will I need to upgrade my plan as my team grows?
- Are features like call recording and shared numbers included in the base plan, or do they cost extra?
- Can I try the system through a demo or free trial?
- Can I pay month to month, or do I have to sign a long-term contract?


**Setup and onboarding**


- How long does setup take for a firm my size?
- Can I keep my existing business number and import client contacts?
- What training or setup help is available for my staff?


**Day-to-day usability**


- Is the system easy to learn and use?
- Can my team take calls from home or when visiting clients?


**Integrations**


- Does the system connect with my practice management or accounting software?
- Does it work with my payment processor?
- Can it integrate with the CRM my firm already uses?


**Security and reliability**


- How does the system protect sensitive client information?
- Can I control which staff members can access call recordings and messages?
- Will clients still be able to reach us if our internet or phone system goes down?


**Support**


- Can I get support by phone, chat, or email?
- When is support available?
- Can I speak to a real person if something goes wrong after hours or on weekends?
